sections.title: 1. Executive Summary and Model Overview
sections.goal: Give senior management, validators and auditors a one-page view of what the model covers, how ECL is calculated and where it is limited. Exposure shown here must reconcile to the general ledger (GL) at the reference date.

c.v: This Model Development Document (MDD) sets out the framework, data, estimation, forward-looking macroeconomic integration and validation results for [Model name] ([Model ID]). The model estimates Expected Credit Loss (ECL) in line with the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition) Directions, 2026 for [funded loans / undrawn commitments / guarantees / debt investments at amortised cost or FVOCI – delete those not in scope]. Assets classified as FVTPL are outside the ECL scope.

For facility i at reporting date t = 0, ECL is the probability-weighted loss across S scenarios over horizons t = 1 … T. T is 12 months for Stage 1 and the remaining expected life for Stage 2 and Stage 3.

ECL(i) = Σ over scenarios s of W(s) × Σ over t = 1..T of [ mPD(i,t,s) × LGD(i,t,s) × EAD(i,t,s) × DF(i,t) ]
DF(i,t) = 1 / (1 + EIR(i))^t
probability of defaulting in interval t, given survival to t − 1, under scenario s.
forward-looking loss given default as a share of EAD at t under scenario s.
projected exposure at t, covering scheduled amortisation, prepayment and undrawn conversion.
discount factor at the instrument’s effective interest rate (EIR).
probability weight of scenario s, with the weights summing to 1.

blocks.text: 5.3 Exposure at default (EAD), prepayment and expected life

c.v: EAD follows the contractual principal schedule plus accrued interest up to the default horizon (typically [3] months of unpaid interest), adjusted for prepayment using a conditional prepayment rate (CPR) modelled by [logistic / vintage survival model].
EAD uses cohort-based credit conversion factors (CCF) by utilisation band and delinquency status:
EAD(t) = Balance(0) + CCF(t) × ( Limit(0) − Balance(0) )

Contractual maturity applies to term loans. For revolving lines without fixed maturity the life is the period over which the bank is exposed to credit risk, capped at [36 / 60] months from empirical attrition and survival curves [attach evidence].
Cash flows are projected at [monthly / quarterly] steps. Marginal PD, LGD and EAD for each step are combined and discounted as in Section 1.2.

sections.title: 6. Forward-Looking Macroeconomic Integration
sections.goal: Show statistical rigour and economic intuition behind each macro variable, and show that multi-scenario weighting captures the non-linearity of losses. The Directions define ECL as the probability-weighted outcome across scenarios.

c.v: Candidate macro series were screened for stationarity (Augmented Dickey-Fuller test), lag structure (0 to 4 quarters), multicollinearity (VIF < 5) and sign consistency. The satellite model links the selected variables to the systemic credit-risk factor Z:
Z(t) = α + β1 × MEV1(t−k) + β2 × MEV2(t−k) + ε(t)
